lattice_filter.rule: For reduced [uvw]: FCC half-integer steps iff u+v+w is even; BCC half-integer steps iff all three are odd; otherwise integer steps. Divide by gcd for unreduced indices.
lattice_filter.scope: Filter reported pure-x lattice-repeat candidates, not measured FFT wavelengths, spatial intervals or row motifs. Compatible means necessary closure only; geometry, mismatch and user choice still apply.

candidate_annotations.reason: P012: local-repeat display score 0.961 = 0.4×row 0.999 + 0.3×strain 0.930 + 0.3×geometry 0.940. This is visual emphasis, not a unique or confirmed period.

policy.meaning: Priority for review based on local repeat evidence; heuristic, not a probability or a selected physical period.
policy.local_association: Within 0.3 NN; exp(-0.5*(distance/tolerance)^2). Keep maximum per grain, average over both grains; channels are correlated, not extra votes.
policy.local_quality: At least 3 observations; strain relative spread <= 0.15. Prominence-stable strain modes weight 1; otherwise 0.5. Only uniformly sampled coordinate rows.
policy.geometry: Mean of 1/(1+(RMS/NN/0.15)^2) for near-GB and non-bulk populations.
policy.highlight_eligibility: Validated pure-x FCC/BCC lattice closure in both grains, positive local row or strain support, both finite geometry residuals, near-GB RMS/NN <= 0.20, at least 3 observable cycles when reported, and no oblique-only role.
policy.tie_break: Equal score to 8 decimals: smaller physical translation first, then candidate id.
policy.count_labels: Upper : lower full a[hkl] coefficients. Display a nominal enumerated pair or allowed FCC/BCC translation-grid pair only when each independently predicted grain length lies within 0.3 NN of the coordinate candidate. Otherwise prefix measured counts with approximation sign; exact measured counts remain separate.
policy.indexing: Validated source orientation when present; otherwise nonnegative descending-index cubic-symmetry representatives for compact display. Original signed PTM directions are preserved in metadata; unresolved directions stay unresolved.

glossary.direction_counts: Labels use full conventional a[hkl] coefficients, upper : lower. Nominal lattice pairs require <=0.3 NN length error in each grain; approximate measured labels use ≈. Original relaxed counts are retained in JSON.
glossary.direction_basis: Validated source directions take precedence. Otherwise compact nonnegative cubic-symmetry representatives are used, preserving original signed PTM directions in JSON; these are not recovered builder orientations.
glossary.near_GB_atoms: Atoms in the surface-excluded interface neighborhood, including the non-bulk core and adjacent crystalline atoms; used to match the complete local pattern.
glossary.non_bulk_core_atoms: Interior interface atoms not assigned to the dominant bulk lattice by PTM; a structural seed set, not all physical GB atoms and not automatically dislocations.
glossary.NN: NN = measured nearest-neighbor distance (2.4883 Å here); RMS/NN is a dimensionless mismatch. Smaller means a closer translated atomic-pattern match.
glossary.highlight: The highlighted candidate has the highest declared review-priority score among eligible local repeats; it is not a probability, a unique physical period, or a user selection.
glossary.long_periods: Long labels indicate evidence for a scale larger than the measured row motif. Coordinate recurrence, local modulation, and field intervals are different evidence; none alone confirms a secondary dislocation or a PBC cell.
glossary.short_periods: Short labels identify measured atomic-row motifs. Associations within 0.3 NN are shown normally; nearby validated lattice candidates within both 0.6 NN and 10% retain their own distinct coordinate length. Neither association claims a Fourier maximum or equality of the two lengths.

nominal_pair_validation.meaning: Upper : lower full a[hkl] coefficients; canonical cubic-symmetry labels are not recovered builder orientations.

short_period_annotations.label: Short structural candidate
short_period_annotations.reason: Repeated atomic-row motif agrees with the coordinate translation; a matching FFT peak is not required.

near.interpretation: A match associates a proposed length with an actual density-spectrum maximum; it does not establish a full xyz repeat.

defects.interpretation: A match associates a proposed length with an actual density-spectrum maximum; it does not establish a full xyz repeat.

short_period_policy.meaning: Observed short row motifs and their associated coordinate candidates; provisional structural scales, not necessarily FFT maxima.
short_period_policy.source: Uniformly sampled atomic rows only; at least three ordinary crest-pair or dominant crest-spacing observations. No supplied target period or integer-multiple inference.
short_period_policy.association: First associate within 0.3 NN. Otherwise search nearby within both 0.6 NN and 10% of the measured row motif; a nearby candidate is distinct from the measured motif, not an equality or FFT confirmation.
short_period_policy.nearby_requirements: Accepted FCC/BCC pure-x indexing in both grains, a nominal lattice pair independently validated at the coordinate translation, near-GB RMS/NN <=0.20, core RMS/NN <=0.25, at least 3 observed cycles, and no oblique-only role.
short_period_policy.nearby_selection: Nearest eligible candidate, then smaller translation and candidate id; all considered nearby alternatives and rejection reasons remain in the annotation. No target ratio is supplied.
short_period_policy.separate_grains: Do not average upper/lower motifs separated by more than 0.3 NN into an unobserved intermediate period.
short_period_policy.none: Missing or unresolved row evidence does not establish that a short structural period is absent.

long_period_policy.meaning: Provisional longer-scale labels for review, not confirmed secondary dislocations or PBC dimensions.
long_period_policy.short_reference_method: Per grain: median ordinary crest-pair length from uniformly sampled alternating rows; otherwise median dominant row-crest spacing. Equal weight per grain.
long_period_policy.scale_separation: At least twice the measured short reference, allowing 0.3 NN association tolerance. No integer-ratio requirement.
long_period_policy.coverage: At least 3 observed cycles, using the minimum of reported candidate cycles and available spatial window / period. Missing coverage does not pass.
long_period_policy.local_evidence: A repeated coordinate-row interruption interval, or prominence-stable strain-spacing modes in both grains; local modes require at least 3 observations and relative spread <= 0.15.
long_period_policy.geometry_supported_local_repeat: Near-GB RMS/NN <= 0.20 and non-bulk RMS/NN <= 0.25 with no oblique-only role. Otherwise retain a field/row interval without calling it a pure-x lattice repeat.
long_period_policy.coordinate_only: Near-GB RMS/NN <= 0.10, core RMS/NN <= 0.15, and mean residual >=20% lower than the nearest distinct candidates on both sides (> half a short reference away). No strain confirmation required.
long_period_policy.repeated_cell_guard: A geometry-only candidate is not a new longer scale if a shorter integer-related candidate has both residuals within 20% of its residuals. Multiples alone do not establish modulation.
long_period_policy.none: No supported longer scale is not proof that none exists; the window or current evidence may be insufficient.

structure_fft_review.method: Retain actual local maxima separated by 0.75 native frequency bins without a global-relative-power threshold. Review uses local prominence, agreement under a half-bin transverse-origin shift, and spectral-shape contrast against each available far-field grain on the same x window/grid. Normalize each spectrum by its total positive-frequency power; this compares power fractions, not absolute scattering intensity, and no spectrum is subtracted. Background is the largest reference power fraction within half a native bin, regularized by max(reference median power fraction, 1e-6 of its largest fraction). These are review heuristics, not statistical significance or evidence of a dislocation.
structure_fft_review.meaning: Background-aware review is heuristic evidence, not a statistical significance test or an identified dislocation period.

strain_fft_review.method: Retain every resolution-separated actual maximum, without a maximum-relative power cutoff or a fixed peak count. Review local prominence and absolute strain amplitude, then require consistent peak frequency/amplitude under a Blackman-window comparison to flag Hann leakage, and actual atom rebinning with a half-x-bin origin shift and neighboring Gaussian smoothing widths. Same-grain far-field signed strain uses the same x window, binning, baseline, z channel and physical power units. Shared far-field peaks are descriptive evidence and never a veto: elastic fields may extend into the far field. These are fixed review heuristics, not significance tests.

policy.window_sensitivity_check: Hann versus Blackman; matched actual peak coherent amplitude ratio must be in [0.5, 2] and exceed the absolute floor

strain_fft_review.meaning: Absolute signed-strain power is comparable across depth and far-field channels; shared far-field peaks are descriptive, never rejected solely for overlap. Local extrema intervals, FFT wavelengths and spatial recurrence remain distinct.

local_strain_spacing_candidates.interpretation: Repeated local spacing of same-sign strain extrema; not necessarily a translation symmetry, Fourier wavelength, or identified dislocation spacing.

policy.single_ratios: Retain every L/S, including failed integer checks; compare the nearest permitted n>=2.
policy.difference_filter: Only distinct long lengths with |(L2-L1)-q*S| <= tolerance, q>=1, are listed.
policy.fractional_offset: ratio - floor(ratio), without snapping the measured ratio to an integer.
policy.relative_errors: Absolute residual divided by the observed L or observed positive L2-L1.
policy.tolerance: Caller-supplied absolute length tolerance; not a confidence interval or a probability.

scale_relations.interpretation: A supported difference relation does not imply integer individual ratios or prove a physical period or dislocation mechanism.
scale_relations.tolerance_policy: 0.3 measured nearest-neighbor distance: a soft numerical association, not a confidence interval or an eligibility gate.

interpretation_limits: All coordinate candidates are retained; a display highlight is not automatic physical identification.
Low-mismatch lattice alternatives and measured structural motifs describe different lengths.
A Fourier peak and recurrence are evaluated separately because local spacings and supercells need not have their own peak.
Bulk atomic density spectra and broad strain averages are not complete descriptors of interfacial spatial motifs.
A strong whole-pattern atomic translation can combine several different local feature intervals.
A fixed percentage of the strongest density peak suppresses weak peaks; geometric far-field references and audited local maxima are recorded separately.

evidence_semantics.fourier_wavelength: Global oscillation of the selected signal; may describe a harmonic, average scale or combination repeat.
evidence_semantics.local_feature_spacing: Consecutive extrema in a stated signed signal, depth and smoothing scale; may vary in space. Not an identified dislocation spacing.
evidence_semantics.atomic_translation: Full-coordinate nearest-atom registration; can fail when the field repeats with transverse phase change.
evidence_semantics.candidate_eligibility: No FFT, recurrence, mismatch or physical scale criterion removes rows from the catalog.
evidence_semantics.structure_fft_review: An actual local maximum is associated by native frequency resolution. Background contrast compares normalized spectral shapes; it is not physical intensity gain or a statistical significance test.
evidence_semantics.strain_fft_review: Actual signed-strain maxima, amplitude and numerical checks are separate from recurrence. A peak shared with a far-field strain profile remains available; shared field evidence is not an automatic rejection.
evidence_semantics.short_motif_association: A nearby indexed coordinate candidate may accompany a measured row motif; both lengths and their discrepancy remain explicit, and a nearby association does not assert equality.
